editorial_opinions.source_text: Ranked ahead of Puka Nacua because Chase combines comparable projected production with the stronger touchdown ceiling and a longer record of elite target dominance. Their frozen statistical projections remain unchanged.

Ranked ahead of Jonathan Taylor because Jeanty’s elite tackle-breaking profile should benefit substantially from Las Vegas’ improved run-game coaching and blocking environment. LineupBeat believes his frozen median projection understates his 2026 ceiling. Their frozen statistical projections remain unchanged.

identity_method: stable GSIS id plus exact normalized name, current team and position; no fuzzy matching

limitations.dst_model: unavailable; model population is QB/RB/WR/TE only
limitations.sportsbook_evidence: private multi-book consensus covers 16 games; qualified exact-player components adjusted 155 projections; raw quotes and lines are not public

methodology.market_policy: High-quality consensus requires at least three books. Team implied-total effects are capped and shrunk to 25%; exact player components are capped to within 25% of the independent model and blended at 25%. Anytime-touchdown prices do not move projections because a one-sided price cannot be safely de-vigged. Raw quotes, prices, lines, and sportsbook identities are never published.
methodology.recommendation_guardrail: A point difference alone cannot create an unqualified recommendation.
methodology.scoring: 0.04/pass yard, 4/pass TD, -2/interception, 0.1/rush or receiving yard, 6/rush or receiving TD, -2/fumble lost, plus format reception points.
methodology.summary: Current Week 1 roster and offensive depth chart × historical team weekly volume × blended historical/current-team and reviewed season-prior player shares; historical and season-prior efficiencies; bounded 2025 opponent and venue adjustments; conservatively shrunk private multi-book game and exact-player consensus inputs.
